name: Windows — Remote Execution via WMI or WinRM
description:
Attacker objective
Execute commands on a remote host over WMI or WinRM/PowerShell-Remoting to move laterally after a foothold.

Attack logic
Remote WMI process creation runs children under WmiPrvSE; WinRM/PS-Remoting runs them under wsmprovhost/winrshost. A shell, scripting host or recon/download tool spawned by these service hosts indicates remote command execution.

Why this detection works
Process-creation lineage ties the WMI/WinRM host process to a suspicious child on the same event, isolating remote execution from local activity.

False positives
Legitimate remote administration and management tooling that uses WMI/WinRM.

Tuning
Allowlist sanctioned management/monitoring source hosts and service accounts; a burst across many destination hosts is higher-risk.

Required telemetry
Process creation with parent process: Sysmon Event ID 1 and Windows Security 4688.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. The parent (WmiPrvSE/wsmprovhost) launched a shell/tool — remote WMI/WinRM execution.
2. Identify the initiating host/user (correlate with 4624 network logons and 5145 shares) and the child command.
3. If unauthorised, treat as lateral movement and isolate both source and destination.
false_positives: Legitimate remote administration and management tooling that uses WMI/WinRM.
query: process where event.code in ("1","4688") and process.parent.name in~ ("wmiprvse.exe","wsmprovhost.exe","winrshost.exe") and process.name in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","cscript.exe","wscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","nltest.exe","schtasks.exe","sc.exe")
